references.text: Moses raises a similar question about his own inadequacy when God calls him to lead Israel out of Egypt.
Moses expresses doubt and resistance to God's call, which is part of the same dialogue where he asks God to send someone else.
Moses claims that he is not eloquent, which is part of his excuses for avoiding the mission God gives him.
The Lord's anger toward Moses because of his resistance, and the solution of sending Aaron as his spokesperson.
Jonah flees from the Lord's call, a similar example of resistance to God's mission.
Jeremiah also expresses reluctance toward God's call by claiming he is too young, similar to Moses' excuses.
Gideon expresses his inadequacy when God calls him, in the same way as Moses.
Isaiah responds to God's call with willingness, in contrast to Moses' reluctance.
Both verses illustrate human resistance to God's immediate call, either by asking for a substitute (Moses) or a delay (the disciple).
Contrast in response to the call: Moses asks for a substitute to avoid the mission, while Paul accepts his mission as sent by God.
The same theme as Luke 9:59: a call met with a desire to postpone obedience due to earthly obligations.
